name: Hochstein
kurzbeschreibung: Mount Hochstein (2,057 m) is Lienz's versatile local adventure mountain in East Tirol, featuring the Schlossbergbahn lifts, the Osttirodler alpine coaster, and Dolomite views.
preis: Mountain trails freely accessible; Schlossbergbahn chairlifts and Osttirodler coaster apply fees
oeffnungszeiten: Summer operations mid-May to late October; lifts and coaster open daily
beschreibung:
Überblick

The commanding summit of Mount Hochstein (2,057 metres) rises directly above the sun-blessed alpine town of Lienz in East Tirol, cherished as one of the region's most versatile activity mountains. Together with its sister peak Zettersfeld across the valley, it forms the core of the Lienzer Bergbahnen network. From its sun-drenched pasture slopes, an expansive 360-degree panorama unfolds across the Lienz basin, the Isel Valley, and the pale limestone towers of the Lienz Dolomites. At the foot of the mountain perches the 13th-century medieval citadel Schloss Bruck, home to prized historical frescoes, while fragrant larch forests climb toward alpine ridges. Hochstein masterfully unites alpine serenity with exhilarating family entertainment: it is world-renowned for the 'Osttirodler', a thrilling 2.7-kilometre all-weather alpine coaster carving through forested loops from the Moosalm plateau directly into the valley.

Route & Anforderungen

The mountain is accessed via three ascending cableway stages or a network of marked alpine hiking trails. Stage one transports visitors from Lienz to the family-friendly Moosalm meadow (1,000 m), home to petting zoos and rustic inns. The upper chairlifts continue via the Sternalm (1,505 m) up to the rustic Hochsteinhütte perched right at the summit ridge (2,023 m). Ambitious mountaineers can climb from the valley floor to the summit cross on foot (approx. 3.5 hours, 1,350 vertical metres). Casual sneakers suffice for strolling around the Moosalm pastures; however, climbing the rocky ridge toward the summit or traversing the high crest to the Böses Weibele peak requires supportive ankle-high boots with vibram rubber traction.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists arrive via highway B100 (Drautalstraße) or B108 (Felbertauernstraße) straight into Lienz. The Schlossbergbahn valley station sits on the western outskirts of the town, offering generous free car parking. By rail, passengers travel to Lienz main station, reaching the lift terminal via local city buses or a pleasant fifteen-minute walk through town.

Tipps

A descent aboard the 'Osttirodler' alpine coaster from the Moosalm is an absolute highlight: the coaster swoops through banked turns with grand views of Schloss Bruck Castle and the jagged Dolomites. Afterward, visit the summit Hochsteinhütte to savor East Tyrolean specialty platters on its panoramic terrace.
